_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
3/16 2:56PM - Good afternoon, Stratton! With rain expected overnight followed by a rapid temperature drop toward sunrise, tomorrow’s operations will look a bit different as we manage a flash freeze across the mountain.

Because the freeze is expected to happen so close to opening hours, surfaces will require grooming before trails are able to open. Our grooming team will begin early in the morning and continue working in sessions throughout the day to manage surfaces and provide the best possible conditions. The plan is for a gradual opening, beginning with 13 groomed trails and 7 lifts scheduled to spin at 9AM, with expected delays due to weather and high winds. We do anticipate limited top to bottom skiing at opening, with additional terrain coming online as grooming progresses and as conditions allow.

Due to the anticipated weather, the Sun Bowl side of the mountain will be closed for the day, and there will be no lift service from that area.

Our operations and grooming teams are no strangers to weather events like this. A great deal of planning and coordination has gone into tomorrow’s approach, with crews tracking trails overnight to help manage the freeze ahead of morning operations. With more stable cold weather expected this week, we look forward to firing up snowmaking tomorrow and begin to rebuild surfaces and expand terrain as we head toward the weekend! 

Be sure to sharpen those edges and tune in frequently throughout the day tomorrow for updates to come.

Safety Tip: Stay on the groomed portion of terrain. 

Looking ahead, next weekend is on fire with HOMESICK taking over the mountain all weekend long. DJ Trevor Andrew will be spinning at 9PM in Grizzly’s for the Welcome Party, and Lunar Laps night skiing will also be available on Friday night. On Saturday, G. Love and DJ Logic presented by IKON Pass and East Street Archives, will be bringing the live music to Grizzly’s. Hope to see you there!
